title: Koine provider architecture
intro: The workflow extension is designed and pending implementation; the baseline views describe the served desktop contract. All providers share one resident Koine process and its native limits. Graphs begin at the node labelled Start here; sequences read from their first message. On narrow screens use native size and pan, the SVG export, or the reflowable spec.

discussion.title: Error channels, event visibility and the unresolved allocation boundary
discussion.status: Feasibility analysis · allocation and subjects remain open
discussion.summary: A public CFError-bearing registration query is a candidate, not proof of bounded internal opens or complete failure reporting. Formatted fs_usage and the local ktrace manual do not establish the required normally signed-host event ledger. Compare direct owned inspection, complete raw observation and private support-process candidates; no runtime mechanism, helper, signing/consent/limit change or reduced workflow guarantee is selected. A passive pre-backoff listener hook is a constructible observation candidate, with actual scheduling and native controls still to design. The resource producer now has separate feasibility, allocation and subject design children. Its complete artifact and the canonical proposal require load-bearing reviews before planning; native, binary and useful-coverage acceptance remains pending.

updatedDiagrams.summary: Adds the source/SDK comparison of metadata health, trace visibility, allocation alternatives and pre-backoff listener observation, with no selected runtime mechanism.

groups.title: Application and file search · designed
groups.description: FIFO and canonical fsgetpath are proposed. Resource feasibility records candidates and limitations; allocation and serviceability-subject design remain open. The complete resource artifact and canonical proposal require review before planning. Typed BLOCKED transport is reviewed; runtime/binary/native coverage and serviceability remain pending.

diagrams.title: Separate metadata health, descriptor bounds and event visibility
diagrams.caption: Source/SDK feasibility only. The CFError-bearing Launch Services candidate does not certify all internal failures or transient descriptor demand. Formatted fs_usage and local ktrace documentation do not establish a complete observer under the approved hardened posture; that is an evidence limit, not proof tracing is impossible. Direct owned inspection and isolated opaque inspection are alternatives requiring design, not accepted runtime routes. Two temporary credits, signed responsibility, infinite/unknown limits and system-wide demand cannot disappear from their contracts. Observe listener errors before NIO suppression; delay/scheduled-read/resumption and real native discriminators remain to construct. Allocation design, serviceability subjects and mandatory review precede planning; native acceptance stays pending.

diagrams.title: Observe one canonical path and diagnose native size refusals
diagrams.caption: Source/SDK-grounded proposal, not native acceptance. fsgetpath takes filesystem/object identity obtained from an owned directory, not the descriptor itself. Before/after identity, mount and parent association checks detect observed changes but do not prevent ABA or check-to-call races. Its 8192-byte buffer counts NUL, preserving at most 8191 directory text bytes; the public 8192-byte value bound still applies to joined file locations. Size omissions need actual-parent proof before finalization, or one root stop. Canonical load-bearing review and signed no-dialog/long-path/identity/native queue subjects remain pending.

diagrams.title: Finish shallow names before bounded descent
diagrams.caption: Proposed per-root FIFO algorithm, not runtime acceptance. Every listing turn uses the canonical observation before reading. Prefix/parent change stops one root; target-only change under stable parent is exact. Name listings occur once, but checked prefix walks repeat against the wait. Depth precedes frontier; frontier omits descendants while anchors remain matchable. Worker-only cleanup retains stream/queue/credits. Canonical review and opaque descriptor/accept-backoff instrument design/review precede planning; measured workflow omissions remain unaccepted.

diagrams.title: Report every root and distinguish blocked scope from failure
diagrams.caption: Designed coverage flow. Atomic busy admission and latched disabled cohorts retain existing CAPACITY_LIMIT/INSPECTION_FAILED meanings. Known native/public path-size omissions use actual-parent VALUE_LIMIT groups before finalization. A formerly fitting prefix now too long is change evidence and stops once, without retroactive name omissions. Counted depth/frontier groups and typed BLOCKED/lifecycle semantics remain. Canonical review and resource instrument design/review precede planning; periodic counts or successful delayed replies cannot certify serviceability.

diagrams.title: Choose a location, then revalidate through existing actions
diagrams.caption: Designed selection handoff. The fsgetpath canonical observation and native bundle identity merge observed routes; distinct installations stay distinct. Size-refused paths are omitted with affecting coverage rather than shortened. Empty/nil opaque metadata alone cannot establish absence or UNREGISTERED. Clients inspect status/coverage/errors before existing actions under both controls. Canonical review and native resource design/review precede planning; binary/native acceptance remains pending.

diagrams.title: Discover names without probing protected traversal
diagrams.caption: Bounded evidence, macOS 26.5/25F71 in a clean TestAnyware VM. Test-only workspace startup instrumentation ran inside the actual signed hardened Koine host with unchanged identity, Info.plist and empty entitlements. Ordinary directory listing, the home scan with exclusions and system-app inspection were prompt-free. Direct Desktop/Documents/Downloads listing and a Desktop Spotlight query prompted. Denial produced Cocoa 257 for listing but an apparently successful zero-result query. Disabled indexing still returned filenames, including from the test disk image. This recommends name enumeration with explicit skipped scope; it proves neither exhaustive discovery nor a race-free no-prompt guarantee. The API and new consent diagnostics remain the next design step.

diagrams.title: First-use metadata and default-handler prompt boundary
diagrams.caption: Measured macOS 26.5/25F71 on a Developer ID hardened GUI probe matching Koine’s empty entitlements and usage keys. Each case resets consent. Metadata and registered-app inspection did not prompt; file-URL handler lookup for text and alias documents did. A TextEdit URL after denial does not establish permission or safe inspection. Protected default opening remains pending a human consent/semantics decision. Removable/network volumes were unavailable. Other workspace operation acceptance remains pending.

diagrams.title: Launch or open, then capture desktop state
diagrams.caption: Designed sequence. All four mutations and their result fields require workspace:control AND desktop:control; neither read is implicit. Unconstrained selection allows running-copy reuse; a path constrains the installation. The receipt carries only optional observed PID/kernel start, for a separately authorized desktop read/focus. The three-second acknowledgment wait can end before Gatekeeper or launch completes, and the core deadline may answer first. An acknowledgment alone does not pass activation acceptance. Reveal returns Finder acknowledgment without a process. App reactions and process/file races remain acceptance limits.

diagrams.title: Keep dependency absence before the submission boundary
diagrams.caption: Designed outcomes after whole-mutation preflight and live admission. Input, capability and inspection failures stay separate; no new OS consent is allocated. Dependency absence certifies only that this action submitted no domain request. After submission a timeout or failure is not a safe retry signal; late acknowledgment is ignored. Without errors at or below the result, AVAILABLE has a receipt and DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE has reason/guidance, never both. Publication errors may suppress the selected branch without changing a published status. Native acknowledgment does not prove browser content, activation or Finder selection.

diagrams.title: Reserve identities and choose before loading
diagrams.caption: Designed startup calculation for each enabled shipped slot, deterministic for fixed verification verdicts. Approval also requires the catalogue's release signing identifier; fixtures use separate test identities. Reserved-only slots cannot load; unrelated claimants cannot evict an absent owner. A highest tie refuses that release group and repeats with remaining eligible copies, reaching the bundle if needed. Every refusal and missing bundle stays visible. Candidate-specific staging preserves quarantine provenance. Ordinary collisions and host/root failures are detailed in the spec. This view is not native verification.

diagrams.title: Keep selection frozen through publication and start
diagrams.caption: Designed lifecycle after selection. Principal conflicts between shipped selections refuse both without fallback; descriptor/schema rejection can leave images mapped but publishes no contribution and can remove authority dependents. Startup failure retains schema and capabilities. No frozen choice is retried. Core management survives provider failure; root/core startup failure can prevent listening. Acceptance uses a fresh host process per native scenario, public GraphQL, and assigned signed VM cases; all remain pending.

diagrams.title: Six providers and their authority boundaries
diagrams.caption: Proposed component composition, not separate deployment containers. Existing desktop grants expand to geometry, pointer and system media; workspace discovery/open, input and menus need distinct grants. All five new bundles use one native loader and the catalogue's release signing identities. Tool operations add any focus/input/menu authority their native effects require. The host association and interaction cleanup algorithms remain downstream design work.

diagrams.title: Capture input or menu targets without desktop control
diagrams.caption: Designed sequence for independently grantable application input or menu actions. Fresh discovery needs that provider's read grant; a previously obtained target can be used with control and a control-authorized receipt. Protected targets are refused again before effects. Bounded system Space switching is a separate operation requiring input and desktop control. References remain provider-local; this view proves no stronger native identity or menu validation.

diagrams.title: Check every effect before dispatching any action
diagrams.caption: Designed host behavior under additional-capabilities-v1. For example, workspace launch/open/reveal requires workspace:control AND desktop:control. Cleanup authority is fixed when an interaction is admitted. An unavailable dependency result certifies no effects by that action, not earlier actions. Protected/stale targets, permission refusal and ambiguous failures remain distinct. The feature needs a compatible framework minor and old/new binary acceptance.

diagrams.title: Resident application and client boundary
diagrams.caption: Runtime responsibility view: one resident Koine application contains the native UI, server and providers. Closing its management window leaves the listener and observation running. The native UI keeps management authority in process; HTTP clients present bearer credentials backed by live grants. Providers share that process and its OS permissions.

diagrams.title: Source packages and interface dependencies
diagrams.caption: Application/framework composition, shown as package dependencies rather than deployment containers. Koine supplies one shared provider framework image, Machine invokes its contracts, and separately built providers conform to them. Published Swift types and protocols carry the compatibility promise; GraphQL-library types remain private. The client owns its GraphQL adapter; no Koine-owned client helper is required.

diagrams.title: Discover windows, derive choices, focus one
diagrams.caption: Served API: query before choices and resolve an opaque reference before acting. Exact targeting is not established across actual PID reuse; see docs/specs/machine.md#native-targeting-discussion. Capability denial and missing Koine consent stay distinct; no automatic mutation replay.

diagrams.title: Authorize every action before executing any
diagrams.caption: Execution flow for an authenticated client operation. The core expands the selected GraphQL operation and checks original schema coordinates, so aliases and fragments do not rename authority. Any denied mutation action prevents all actions from beginning. Revocation is checked again at each dispatch admission. Earlier authorized effects are not rolled back if a later action fails. Enrollment and the in-process console have separately defined admission cases in the spec.

diagrams.title: Grant issuance, approval and revocation
diagrams.caption: Bearer-credential lifecycle and revocation ordering. Anonymous enrollment creates only a pending request. Existing managers or the in-process console approve requests or create manual grants. Approved grants survive restart without automatic expiry; pending-request expiry does not expire them. Secret possession permits own-request status before and after its decision; revoked grants fail authentication. Digest uniqueness prevents retries from creating multiple grants. Already admitted actions may finish. This diagram is not a model-checking result.

diagrams.title: Swift framework and the rejected alternative
diagrams.caption: Koine uses the shared resilient Swift framework. Swift types and protocols are part of its stable published contract, with library evolution and module stability enabled. Koine does not use the C-compatible alternative. Compatible provider binaries dynamically link the host-supplied framework; newer required symbols need a newer host and are checked before loading.

diagrams.title: Native schema and resolver contributions
diagrams.caption: The shared Swift framework as the loader applies it. Verify signed manifests and required framework versions before loading, then resolve the named principal class and require ProviderFactory conformance. Validate schema and authority metadata before starting the Provider. Requests/results use owned Swift values and async protocol methods. Independently built old/new binaries are verified through the native plugin seam (docs/verification/binary-compatibility.md); native trust is distinct from client capabilities.
